note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see researcher_us/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

findings.finding: The Q3 revenue bar of about $126.5M is +6.1% on Q2's $119.2M, but in the same quarter last year Vyjuvek grew only +1.9% q/q ($96.0M to $97.8M), and management then cited summer therapy pauses and 'a bit lower' US sales. That year's consensus had modelled a q/q decline ($93.7M against $96.0M), and the quarter beat by 4.4%. This year's consensus assumes no summer dip on a US base of $91.6M, so a repeat of the seasonal pattern lands the quarter around $121-124M, a 2-4% miss.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue misses: Q1 2025 -10.6% on revenue gave -14.06% (2025-05-06); Q2 2026 -1.4% on revenue gave -8.37% (2026-08-03). Beats: Q3 2025 +4.4% gave +0.17%; Q4 2025 +1.7% gave +4.12%. Revenue misses are sold hard and beats bought mildly.

findings.finding: Germany's AMNOG price negotiation for Vyjuvek should conclude around the Q3 print. The G-BA decision came on 2026-02-19 (procedure start 2025-08-15), so the six-month negotiation ran to about 2026-08-19. On the Q2 call management said it expected completion in Q3 and called its accrual 'conservative'. A full quarter of German price reserve had kept Q2 ex-US revenue flat at $27.6M (vs $28.9M in Q1), with 'maybe a partial' reserve in Q3 and normal German net revenue by Q4. The outcome, a final price at or above the accrual (reserve release, clean ex-US run-rate) or arbitration by the Schiedsstelle (overhang persists), is likely disclosed in the Q3 release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: ex-US revenue went flat on the German reserve and total revenue missed by 1.4%; the stock fell 8.37% on 2026-08-03. No earlier price-resolution event to compare against.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 was a benign catastrophe quarter by the industry's own counts. Gallagher Re puts 9M26 global insured cat losses at $92bn, the lowest since 2019, with no single event over $10bn and a slow Atlantic season. Hurricane Isaias landed 9 Oct, outside Q3. CNA's Q2 2026 had $60M of pretax cats (2.3 pts) and the CNA bar ($1.19-1.23) is roughly a repeat of Q2's $1.19, so a light Q3 cat load leans toward meeting or beating that bar. Against Q3 2025's very low $41M, though, peers' cats rose year on year (Travelers $538M vs $302M; W.R. Berkley ~$86M vs ~$79M), mainly from severe convective storms.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Loews has not traded on CNA cat lines: Q3 2025 (CNA core record $1.50, cats $41M) moved -0.14% on 2025-11-03; Q2 2026 moved +0.21% (baseline).

findings.finding: Commercial middle-market loss trends worsened at peers in Q3 2026, and that is CNA's core book. Hartford's Middle & Large Business underlying combined ratio was 99.5, against 91.4 a year earlier and 95.3 in Q2 2026, on workers' comp and non-cat property; the trade press reported it on 2026-10-27 as a trend, not a one-off. Chubb's North America commercial combined ratio worsened to 86.3 from 81.5, with $13M of unfavorable long-tail development. CNA already raised its 2026 underlying loss picks in Q2 (underlying combined ratio 94.2 vs 91.7), so further deterioration would come on top of that.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Loews's largest move in the baseline, -5.86% on 2026-05-04, came when CNA's combined ratio rose to 102.2% on a $106M reserve charge plus a 2.6-pt underlying loss-ratio increase (https://rallies.ai/news/loews-drops-after-q1-profit-declines-as-cna-reserve-charge-hits-underwriting-results). Q2 2026 brought a 2.5-pt underlying increase with no PYD, and the stock moved +0.21%.

findings.finding: Q3 is when CNA books its annual Life & Group reserve review, a one-off inside the print. The last two were small: Q3 2025 LTC assumption update +$7M pretax to reserves (about $7M after-tax hit to core per the release), and Q3 2024 +$15M pretax. CNA also did a $1bn LTC portfolio trade in Q2 2026 that extended duration. Nothing points to a large Q3 2026 update, but this is the one scheduled reserve event in the quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 (LTC update ~$7M) moved -0.14%; Q3 2024's update was $15M pretax. Neither shows a reaction attributable to the review.

findings.finding: Loews Hotels faces a weaker Q3 at its biggest market. Comcast reported on 2026-10-22 that Theme Parks Q3 2026 revenue fell 4.4% to $2,597M and Adjusted EBITDA fell 17.1% to $780M, on lower admissions and more promotions, and said Orlando softness would continue into Q4 and 1H27. Loews Hotels' Universal Orlando JV hotels drove its Q2 2026 Adjusted EBITDA up 26% to $137M. The Q3 2025 comparison is $69M Adjusted EBITDA (+8%), and the three new Orlando hotels are no longer an incremental year-on-year driver. Net of the rest of the company: hotels are about $69M of EBITDA in a quarter where CNA plus Boardwalk earn about $400M after tax to Loews, so even a 20% hotel miss is roughly $0.05 a share.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Hotels have never been the reaction line. Q1 2026 hotels Adjusted EBITDA +53% came with a -5.86% move driven by CNA; Q2 2026 hotels +26% came with +0.21%.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 equity returns were weak outside mega-caps: S&P 500 total return +2.3% but equal-weight -1.87% (Morgan Stanley), against a very strong Q3 2025. That leans against CNA's limited-partnership and common-stock income, which was $131M in Q2 2026 and $71M in Q3 2025, and against the parent's trading portfolio. Loews's Q3 2025 corporate segment earned $42M, already down on lower trading income, and the parent's trading fixed maturities shrank to $291M at 2026-06-30 from $633M at year end, so the parent leg is smaller now.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Investment-income swings have not been isolated as a reaction line. Q3 2025 (record CNA core, corporate down) moved -0.14%.

findings.finding: Loews's buyback pace has been slow in 2026: $179M for 1H26, of which $146M (1.4M shares) came in Q2. findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Buyback figures are disclosed every quarter and have never moved the stock measurably. Q2 2026's $146M came with +0.21%.

findings.finding: Three peers that reported after Marriott's last update (2026-08-03) printed Q3 RevPAR far above Marriott's own Q3 global guide of +3.5% to +4.0%. Hilton system +5.8% with US +7.0%, Europe +6.5% and MEA -5.6% (8-K, 2026-10-27). Hyatt comparable system +7.2% with US +8.2%, luxury leading, and the FY RevPAR guide raised to +5.0-5.5% (8-K, 2026-10-29). IHG global +5.3% with Americas +6.8% (2026-10-22). Marriott's US & Canada is about two-thirds of its system and luxury/upper-upscale heavy, and CoStar put luxury/upper-upscale RevPAR at about +10.2% from Memorial Day to Labor Day. That implies Marriott Q3 global RevPAR of roughly +5%, about 1.25pt above the top of its guide, and a mechanical FY RevPAR raise from 3.0-3.5% to about 3.75-4.25%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-08-03 Marriott beat EPS ($3.19 vs ~$3.05) and raised FY RevPAR, and the stock fell -6.97% on a revenue miss. On 2026-02-10 the stock rose +8.5% and on 2025-11-04 +3.16% (baseline). Peers this week: Hilton beat RevPAR, raised FY RevPAR and fell -2.1% on Oct 27. Hyatt beat by more, raised FY RevPAR by about a point and rose +6.3% on Oct 29 (Yahoo daily closes).

findings.finding: The Q4/FY guide is exposed to the Middle East in its peak quarter and to the midterms. Marriott said on its Q2 call that Q4 is normally about 35% of its Middle East full-year revenue, that Q4 2025 had big ADR-lifting events, and that Q4 RevPAR would be 'a bit lower than Q3'. Hilton (2026-10-27) guided Q4 RevPAR to only +3.0-3.5%, flagged an 'increased impact from the Middle East' and cut its FY EBITDA expectation for the Middle East and timeshare fees despite raising RevPAR, and its stock fell 2.1% that day. Accor said UAE RevPAR was still about -20% year on year in Q3 (2026-10-22). Marriott has the largest Gulf footprint of the US majors, so a Q4 fee/EBITDA guide below the Street and an FY EBITDA raise smaller than the RevPAR beat implies is a real risk.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-08-03 a raised FY RevPAR guide, with NUG at the low end on Middle East construction delays and investment spending raised, was sold -6.97% (baseline; https://finviz.com/news/375971/marriott-shares-slip-despite-earnings-beat-as-revenue-falls-short-of-expectations). Peer on the same line this week: Hilton -2.1% on a Q4 guide dragged by the Middle East.

findings.finding: US demand stayed strong into Q4, which supports the US half of the guide. US hotel RevPAR was +5.5% in the week of 11-17 October 2026 (occupancy +3.1%, ADR +2.3%; CoStar via Hospitality Net, published 2026-10-23), after +14.2% in the week of 20-26 September on the Rosh Hashanah shift. Hyatt cited 'momentum after Labor Day' in raising its FY guide. This sits against Hilton's Q4 system guide of +3.0-3.5% and gives Marriott room for a firmer US Q4 comment than Hilton gave.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not separately observable for Marriott. Hyatt's post-Labor Day momentum comment came with a raise and +6.3% on Oct 29.

The last time it entered a print after a run, with a guide raise in hand (2026-08-03), it fell 6.97%.

findings.finding: New Chase and American Express US co-brand card deals were expected to add about $30M of fees in H2 2026, with global card fees up in the high-30% range for 2026. This is already in the FY guide (Q2 call), and Japan yen weakness partly offsets it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The co-brand deal announcement drove a re-rating earlier in 2026 (https://rallies.ai/news/marriott-rallies-as-analysts-re-rate-stock-on-richer-credit-card-royalties-and-2026-outlook). Not visible as a print line since.

findings.finding: The owner dispute over Bonvoy economics is unresolved. 51 owners representing nearly 1,000 hotels wrote to leadership (reported by the WSJ 2026-06-16) asking for a share of card fees. On the Q2 call management cut charge-out rates about 5%, raised award-night reimbursement and added an incentive of up to 50bp of room revenue, but declined to respond formally. Further concessions or cost (the incentive sits in owned/leased and other) could show up in Q3 margins or Q4 commentary.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on this line. Owned/leased guidance has been cut twice (Earnings Whispers preview).

findings.finding: China and APAC look soft against Marriott's FY Greater China guide of +2-3%. In Q3, IHG Greater China RevPAR was -3.3% (weather, holiday timing), Hilton Asia Pacific -0.5%, and Accor said China declined, while Hyatt Greater China was +2.1%. Marriott's Greater China is a meaningful share of international rooms, so a Q3 China print near zero and a trimmed China guide are plausible.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not observed as a driver of Marriott's last reactions, which turned on the US and the Middle East.

findings.finding: Net rooms growth was guided to the low end of 4.5-5% because of Middle East construction delays, against Hilton's 6-7% (reiterated at the midpoint 2026-10-27), and 2026 investment spending was raised to $1.25-1.35B on key money. A further NUG trim would extend the unit-growth gap to Hilton.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The NUG trim in August came with a -6.97% day, though the release-day coverage pinned that day on the revenue miss.

lessons_applied: 'What has worked' (a peer's print landing after the company last spoke, leaving consensus stale): the peer RevPAR read-through went from +1.0 to +1.2. Lesson 1 (this name sold its August beat for -7%) is already in that size, so it is not cut twice.
Lesson 1 / core table (apply each lesson once): the positioning/run-up finding went from -0.8 to -0.6, because the beat-selling reaction function was already applied to the reported-quarter finding.

Asking 'what did the market miss' generates pessimism: draft sum -0.8 checked against the evidence. The US data is strongly positive, so p_up moved from 48 to 49 and the scaled number from -0.18 to -0.09.
